description: AfriScope is a solo project for the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026 (Be An Earth System Trend Detective!). The initiative investigates long-term climate change across Africa by analyzing and comparing historical environmental data—specifically temperature trends—across major African cities and regions representing North, West, East, Central, and Southern Africa.
summary:
AfriScope is an independently developed, data-driven project that explores climate trends and potential environmental risks across ten major African cities from 1991 to 2025. Using NASA POWER Earth observation data, the project analyzes three key climate indicators: temperature, rainfall, and root-zone soil moisture.

I developed a data analysis methodology using Python, Microsoft Excel, Power Query, and Power Pivot to process historical climate records, calculate annual averages, measure variability, and identify long-term trends. By combining these indicators, AfriScope explores how changing temperatures, rainfall patterns, and soil moisture conditions may reveal emerging environmental pressures across different African regions.

The project addresses the challenge by transforming NASA climate data into meaningful, comparable insights. It is important because understanding regional climate patterns can raise awareness, support informed decisions, and encourage climate resilience across Africa.
details:
AfriScope is a data-driven project that analyzes climate trends and potential environmental risks across ten major African cities between 1991 and 2025. Using NASA POWER data, the project examines three key variables: temperature, rainfall, and root-zone soil moisture.

Through Python, Excel, Power Query, and Power Pivot (DAX), AfriScope processes historical climate data and applies statistical analysis to identify long-term trends, annual variability, and differences between cities.

By combining these three climate indicators, the project aims to identify emerging environmental pressures, improve understanding of climate variability across Africa, and support climate awareness and resilience planning. Its findings will be presented through accessible data visualizations, making complex NASA Earth observation data easier to understand and explore.

AfriScope — Seeing Africa's Climate Through Data.
